A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SenseNova-SI study. Their text, tables, figures, algorithm and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised and added material.

before.justification: v3 reports original trained-model evaluations, scaling experiments, shortcut tests, CoT comparisons and simulated robotic-manipulation results.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, capability-transfer experiments, text-only training controls and a GRPO experiment.

M1.justification: Section 5.6 adds an experimental training variant that applies GRPO reinforcement learning after CoT-SenseNova-SI-CGMap. The main model architectures, data-curation algorithm and stated one-epoch training recipe remain unchanged; this is a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Spatial evaluation expands from five benchmarks to eight through BLINK, 3DSR and EmbSpatial, adding perceptual, varied-viewpoint and embodied-scene coverage. General evaluation expands from four benchmarks in v3 Table 8 to nine in v4 Table 9, adding DocVQA, MMVP, V*, MMMU and Video-MME. The main training-data coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The main spatial comparator roster is retained, but individual comparisons change. Table 3 adds Gemini-3-Pro-Preview to the circular/no-vision tests. The general-capability comparison drops Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B, MindCube, SpatialLadder and SpaceR between v3 Table 8 and v4 Table 9; additional MMBench-EN comparators formerly in Table 1 are also absent.

E3.justification: Table 1 now reports EASI-8 evaluation throughout, replacing the earlier exceptions for paper-quoted baseline results. New designs include capability-specific training on over one million examples, paired 800K visual/text-only training, and 3DSR circ_eval. Table 4 introduces full-set QA+CoT and GRPO conditions and replaces relative-direction difficulty breakdowns with a VSI-Bench summary, although accompanying prose still describes subset evaluation.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests transfer from isolated MM, SR and PT training; new Appendix G compares visual and text-only training to investigate shortcuts. Section 5.6 extends the CoT analysis to full-set training and GRPO, while removing the previous difficulty-stratified results. Table 3 also extends the existing robustness analysis to Gemini-3-Pro-Preview.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same ±0.5-standard-deviation bands described in Figure 1 and Appendix A. No new repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Numerous results are added, replaced or removed. For example, Table 1 changes SenseNova-SI-Qwen3-VL-8B's VSI/MindCube scores from 62.9/74.8 to 64.8/73.8. New results cover eight additional benchmarks and the transfer/text-only controls; Table 4 reports 49.2 for full-set CogMap training and 43.1 after GRPO. Changed conditions prevent treating all replacements as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The capability definitions, normalization description and mathematical content of Algorithm 1 are retained. The added transfer matrix and GRPO experiment introduce no new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The introduction extends the claim that CoT fails to reliably improve spatial reasoning beyond QA scaling to include reinforcement learning. The central contributions concerning data scaling, spatial generalization and downstream utility remain substantially the same.

C2.justification: v4 links unsuccessful GRPO training to long-CoT inconsistencies and interprets the new text-only controls as evidence of visual dependence and MMSI's resistance to language shortcuts. Section 5.6 removes v3's explicit warning that definitive conclusions are premature. The existing qualitative CoT failure explanations remain in the renamed Appendix J.

D1.justification: v4 identifies the report as describing SenseNova-SI v1.1, supplies data budgets for the new controls, and repairs JSON bracing in the documented embodied-agent prompt. The core hardware, optimizer, learning rate, batch size and code/model access links are retained. Detailed GRPO implementation settings are not supplied.

R1.justification: References are added for the new benchmarks, DeepSeekMath/GRPO and SpatialReasoner. Section 5.6 explicitly relates its RL interpretation to SpatialReasoner. The main related-work organization and positioning of data scaling relative to 3D-expert approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, consolidates benchmark descriptions, merges the Main Results subsections and lightly rewrites the conclusion. New appendix sections are inserted, but most existing explanations, data-curation documentation and case studies remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains an average and three spatial-benchmark columns while moving general evaluation to the appendix. The general-capability table expands from four to nine benchmarks, and Table 4 is substantially reorganized. Five new tables present transfer, text-only training and detailed added-benchmark results. The embodied prompt is also reformatted across two pages.

improvement.justification: The capability-transfer and matched text-only training controls strengthen the evidence about transfer and visual dependence, while broader evaluations reveal useful limitations. These provide a limited net improvement over v3. Benefits are tempered by reduced general-baseline coverage, Table 4's mismatch with retained subset-evaluation prose, and insufficient qualification of capability-retention claims despite new losses in Table 9, such as DocVQA 92.1 for base InternVL3-8B versus 84.9 after training.
